questions.q: All of the following are components of the juxtaglomerular apparatus EXCEPT:
questions.exp: JGA components: JG cells, macula densa and mesangial/lacis/supporting (Polkissen) cells; podocytes are glomerular, not JGA. (Book p726)

questions.q: Fill up: The macula densa is composed of modified tall ______ cells.
questions.exp: Macula densa composition: modified tall columnar cells. (Book p726)

questions.q: Fill up: The macula densa sits in the cortical portion of the thick ascending limb (TAL), also called the distal ______ tubule.
questions.exp: Site: cortical portion of thick ascending limb of loop of Henle (TAL)/distal straight tubule. (Book p726)

questions.q: Tubulo-glomerular (TG) feedback by the macula densa is mediated by:
questions.exp: Function of macula densa: TG feedback mediated by adenosine. (Book p726)

questions.q: Match each macula densa fact with its detail — 1) Composition 2) Site 3) Function … A) TG feedback mediated by adenosine B) Modified tall columnar cells C) Cortical TAL / distal straight tubule
questions.exp: Macula densa: modified tall columnar cells (composition) in the cortical TAL/distal straight tubule (site), doing TG feedback via adenosine (function). (Book p726)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the macula densa is TRUE?
opts: It lies in the cortical portion of the thick ascending limb / distal straight tubule
It lies in the medullary portion of the thin descending limb
It lies in the proximal convoluted tubule
It lies within the glomerular capillary tuft
questions.exp: Site of macula densa: cortical portion of TAL/distal straight tubule, where it senses tubular load. (Book p726)

questions.q: In the JG-apparatus figure, the arteriole labelled leaving the glomerulus beside the smooth-muscle layer is the:
questions.exp: The JG apparatus figure labels the efferent arteriole with its smooth muscle layer, plus internal elastic lamina, glomerular epithelium, JG cells, basement membrane, distal tubule (straight) and macula densa. (Book p726)

questions.q: Match each label in the JG apparatus figure with where its leader points — 1) Internal elastic lamina 2) Glomerular epithelium 3) Basement membrane … A) Wall of the distal tubule in cross-section B) Top wall of the arteriole C) Covering of the glomerular tuft
questions.exp: Internal elastic lamina → top arteriole wall; glomerular epithelium → tuft covering; basement membrane → distal tubule wall. (Book p726)

questions.q: All of the following are labelled in the JG apparatus figure EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The figure labels distal tubule (straight), macula densa and JG cells (with efferent arteriole, smooth muscle layer, internal elastic lamina, glomerular epithelium and basement membrane); no thin ascending limb. (Book p726)

questions.q: In the sequence-of-tubular-injury table, the phase of tubular injury lasts:
questions.exp: Phase 1 (tubular injury): duration < 24 hrs. (Book p726)

questions.q: A patient started on gentamicin develops renal tubular injury with PCT damage in under 24 hours. In the book's phase-1 MOA, gentamicin is the example of:
questions.exp: Renal tubular injury from tubulotoxic drugs (eg. gentamicin) → PCT injury within < 24 hrs. (Book p726)

questions.q: Fill up: In phase 1, PCT injury lowers reabsorption of solute + H2O and increases their loss in ______.
questions.exp: ↓ reabsorption of solute + H2O → ↑ loss of solute + H2O in urine. (Book p726)

questions.q: All of the following are findings of the TG-feedback phase EXCEPT:
questions.exp: TG-feedback phase findings: ↓GFR, ↑S.creatinine, ↑K+ → cardiac arrhythmias, ↑H+ → metabolic acidosis; GFR falls, not rises. (Book p726)

questions.q: In the TG-feedback phase, the raised H+ load leads to:
questions.exp: Phase-2 findings: ↑H+ → metabolic acidosis (with ↓GFR, ↑S.creatinine and ↑K+ → cardiac arrhythmias). (Book p726)

questions.q: Match each sensing priority of the macula densa with the ion — 1) First sensed 2) Second sensed 3) Third sensed … A) Na+ B) Cl- C) K+
questions.exp: Macula densa senses Cl- > K+ > Na+ load delivered to the TAL. (Book p726)

questions.q: Fill up: Sensing the increased tubular load, the macula densa triggers release of ______, which constricts the afferent arteriole.
questions.exp: Impaired reabsorption → macula densa senses load → release of adenosine → constricts afferent arteriole. (Book p726)

questions.q: The management listed for the TG-feedback phase of tubular injury is:
opts: Supportive care with monitored fluid intake
questions.exp: Mx: supportive care; monitor fluid intake (↑ chance of edema due to renal failure). (Book p727)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the TG-feedback MOA is TRUE?
opts: Afferent arteriolar constriction lowers GFR (glomerular filtration rate) and prevents further salt + H2O loss
Afferent constriction raises GFR to flush the tubule
Efferent dilatation is the protective step
The feedback increases urinary salt loss
questions.exp: Constricts afferent arteriole → ↓GFR (glomerular filtration rate) → ↑S.creatinine and prevents further salt + H2O loss due to impaired reabsorption. (Book p727)

questions.q: In the sequence-of-tubular-injury table, the MOA column for the recovery phase (3) shows:
questions.exp: Row 3 'Recovery phase' carries only a dash in the MOA column. (Book p727)

questions.q: A patient with prolonged vomiting becomes dehydrated and develops pre-renal failure. The first event in the book's chain is:
questions.exp: Dehydration (eg. ↑ vomiting → pre-renal failure) begins with loss of intravascular volume. (Book p727)

questions.q: Fill up: Loss of intravascular volume lowers glomerular ______ pressure and therefore GFR.
questions.exp: Loss of intravascular volume → ↓ glomerular hydrostatic pressure → ↓ GFR. (Book p727)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the dehydration chain is TRUE?
opts: Proximal tubular absorption increases and feeds the macula densa signal
Proximal tubular absorption falls to zero
The macula densa senses an increased Na+/Cl-/K+ load
The afferent arteriole constricts in this chain
questions.exp: ↑ proximal tubular absorption (+) → macula densa senses ↓Na+/Cl-/K+ → dilatation of afferent arteriole. (Book p727)

questions.q: Fill up: In dehydration, afferent arteriolar dilatation that restores GFR is mediated by ______.
questions.exp: Dilatation of afferent arteriole is mediated by prostaglandins → ↑ GFR. (Book p727)

questions.q: The final outcome of the dehydration/TG-feedback chain is:
questions.exp: Prostaglandin-mediated afferent dilatation ends with ↑ GFR. (Book p727)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the book's AKI cause groups is TRUE?
opts: Inside-kidney causes are ATI/ATN and acute interstitial nephritis
Pre-renal causes arise inside the kidney
Post-renal causes arise inside the kidney
questions.exp: Outside kidney = pre-renal + post-renal; inside kidney = ATI/ATN + AIN. (Book p727)

questions.q: Match each AKI cause group with its members — 1) Outside kidney 2) Inside kidney … A) ATI/ATN and acute interstitial nephritis B) Pre-renal and post-renal causes
opts: Both groups contain only pre-renal causes
questions.exp: Outside kidney = pre-renal + post-renal; inside kidney = ATI/ATN + AIN. (Book p727)

questions.q: Fill up: JG cells are composed of ______ cells.
questions.exp: JG cells composition: granular cells. (Book p727)

questions.q: Fill up: JG cells sit in the tunica ______ of the afferent arteriole (more than the efferent).
questions.exp: Site: tunica media of afferent arteriole > efferent arteriole. (Book p727)

questions.q: The function of JG cells is to:
questions.exp: JG cell function: produce renin. (Book p727)

questions.q: All of the following stimulate JG cells to release renin EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The stimulator diagram shows ↓ renal perfusion pressure, prostaglandins and β1-receptors all (+) JG cells → renin; raised perfusion pressure does not. (Book p728)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about renin release is TRUE?
opts: β1-receptor stimulation acts positively on JG cells
Renin is released by macula densa cells
questions.exp: β1-receptors (with prostaglandins and ↓ perfusion pressure) positively stimulate JG cells to secrete renin. (Book p728)

questions.q: A patient on a β-blocker shows blunted renin release during hypovolemia. The receptor through which the book's stimulator diagram drives renin release is:
questions.exp: β1-receptors (with prostaglandins and ↓ renal perfusion pressure) act positively on JG cells → renin, so β-blockade blunts the response. (Book p728)

questions.q: The renal artery is described in the circulation chain as a:
questions.exp: Renal circulation starts: renal artery (end artery). (Book p728)

questions.q: The renal artery divides into how many segmental arteries, in what arrangement?
questions.exp: Renal artery → 5 segmental arteries (4 anterior + 1 posterior). (Book p728)

questions.q: Match each arterial station with the next vessel it gives — 1) Segmental arteries 2) Interlobar arteries 3) Arcuate arteries … A) Arcuate arteries B) Interlobular/cortical radial arteries C) Interlobar arteries
questions.exp: Segmental → interlobar → arcuate → interlobular/cortical radial → afferent arteriole. (Book p728)

questions.q: Fill up: The afferent arteriole supplies the glomerular capillary plexus located in the ______.
questions.exp: Afferent arteriole supplies glomerular capillary plexus (in cortex). (Book p728)

questions.q: Fill up: Blood leaves the glomerular capillary plexus through the ______ arteriole.
questions.exp: Glomerular plexus → efferent arteriole → peritubular capillary plexus. (Book p728)

questions.q: Medullary blood supply in the circulation chain is mediated by the:
questions.exp: Peritubular capillary plexus → blood supply to medulla (mediated by vasa recta). (Book p728)

questions.q: Fill up: The venous return runs: descending limb → ascending limb of vasa recta → renal vein → ______.
questions.exp: Ascending limb of vasa recta → renal vein → IVC (inferior vena cava). (Book p728)

questions.q: All of the following follow the book's forward circulation order EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Forward order is interlobar → arcuate (not arcuate → interlobar); the other pairs follow the chain as written. (Book p728)

questions.q: Match each renal zone with its blood supply — 1) Cortex 2) Medulla … A) Vasa recta with poor supply B) Renal artery with good supply
opts: Both supplied equally by renal artery
questions.exp: Cortex: supplied by renal artery, good supply; medulla: supplied by vasa recta, poor supply. (Book p728)

questions.q: Fill up: Within the poorly supplied medulla, the segment m/c vulnerable to hypoxia is the pars recta / proximal ______ tubule.
questions.exp: Medulla: poor supply; pars recta/proximal straight tubule is m/c vulnerable to hypoxia. (Book p728)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about renal zone perfusion is TRUE?
opts: The medulla has a poor supply delivered by vasa recta
The medulla has a richer supply than the cortex
The cortex is supplied by vasa recta
Both zones are equally vulnerable to hypoxia
questions.exp: Cortex = renal artery, good supply; medulla = vasa recta, poor supply with the pars recta m/c vulnerable to hypoxia. (Book p728)

questions.q: Match each label in the vascularity-of-nephron figure with the structure it names — 1) Afferent arteriole 2) Proximal convoluted tubule 3) Glomerular capsule … A) Vessel entering the glomerular tuft B) Cup around the glomerular tuft C) Tubule segment coiling beside the glomerulus
questions.exp: Afferent arteriole enters the tuft; proximal convoluted tubule coils beside the glomerulus; glomerular capsule cups the tuft. (Book p728)

questions.q: In the vascularity figure, the red vessel ascending beside the tubule and the blue vessel with its small tributary are labelled:
opts: Interlobular artery, and interlobular vein with venule
Interlobar artery, and interlobar vein with venule
Arcuate artery, and arcuate vein with venule
Segmental artery, and segmental vein with venule
questions.exp: Figure labels: interlobular artery (red) with interlobular vein and its venule (blue). (Book p728)

questions.q: All of the following are labelled in the 'Vascularity of nephron' figure EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Figure labels: glomerular capsule, efferent/afferent arterioles, proximal convoluted tubule, interlobular artery, venule, interlobular vein, loop of the nephron, peritubular capillary network — no macula densa. (Book p728)

questions.q: In the vascularity-of-nephron note, the efferent arteriole is sandwiched between the:
opts: Glomerular capillary plexus and peritubular capillary plexus
questions.exp: Efferent arteriole is sandwiched b/w glomerular capillary plexus and peri-tubular capillary plexus. (Book p728)

questions.q: At the bottom of the vascularity figure, urine flows into the:
questions.exp: Figure annotation: urine flows into renal papilla. (Book p728)

questions.q: In the renal-diseases note, tubules and interstitium make up what share of the kidney?
questions.exp: Renal diseases tree: tubules & interstitium 85% of kidney; vascular 5%. (Book p729)

questions.q: In AKI (hours to days), match each lesion with its m/c cause — 1) ATN 2) AIN … A) Drug hypersensitivity B) Ischemia
questions.exp: AKI (hours to days): ATN d/t ischemia (m/c); AIN d/t drug hypersensitivity (m/c). (Book p729)

questions.q: Fill up: Chronic tubulointerstitial fibrosis/disease (the CKD arm) leads to RTA type ______.
questions.exp: CKD: chronic tubulointerstitial fibrosis/disease → RTA type 4. (Book p729)

questions.q: Match each vascular disorder class with its disease — 1) Large vessel disorders 2) Small vessel disorders … A) TMA (thrombotic microangiopathy) B) RAS (renal artery stenosis)
questions.exp: Vascular (5%): large vessel disorders → RAS (renal artery stenosis); small vessel disorders → TMA. (Book p729)

questions.q: Small vessel disorders (TMA) progress through which sequence to chronic kidney disease?
questions.exp: Small vessel disorders → TMA → hypertensive crisis → progress to CKD (ischemic nephropathy). (Book p729)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the vascular arm of renal disease is TRUE?
opts: It accounts for 5% of the kidney and includes large- and small-vessel disorders
It accounts for 85% of the kidney
questions.exp: Vascular = 5% of kidney with large vessel (RAS) and small vessel (TMA → hypertensive crisis → ischemic nephropathy) disorders; 85% and RTA-4 belong to the tubulointerstitial arm. (Book p729)

questions.q: All of the following belong to the vascular (5%) arm of the renal-diseases tree EXCEPT:
opts: Hypertensive crisis progressing to ischemic nephropathy
questions.exp: ATN d/t ischemia sits in the tubules & interstitium (85%) arm under AKI; the vascular arm holds RAS, TMA and hypertensive crisis. (Book p729)
